close_reason: Shipped. from_pem_file / from_der_file now route through read_file_capped(path, DEFAULT_FILE_SIZE_CAP) (64 MiB). Two-stage check: metadata().len() short-circuits multi-GB files, Read::take(cap+1) defends against TOCTOU and /dev/zero-style infinite streams. Oversized inputs surface as Error::Io with ErrorKind::InvalidData (MSRV 1.73 predates ErrorKind::FileTooLarge from Rust 1.83) plus a 'exceeds N-byte cap' message. Public escape hatches: from_pem_file_with_cap / from_der_file_with_cap. 5 new integration tests in tests/file_size_cap.rs cover oversized-reject, under-cap-pass, default-cap-pin. Workspace tests + clippy --all-features -D warnings + rustdoc -D warnings clean.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:397-400 (from_pem_file) and :410-413 (from_der_file) both call fs::read(path) which loads the entire file into a Vec<u8> with no size limit.

Trigger paths:
- Caller passes a path that resolves to /dev/zero, /dev/random, or a FIFO that streams forever -> the process hangs or OOMs.
- Caller passes a path to a multi-GB file (a corrupted bundle, an accidentally-symlinked log file, an attacker-influenced env var like SSL_CERT_FILE pointing at a junk file) -> unbounded heap allocation, possible OOM-kill.
- Sibling adapter crates (pkix-truststore-system) may consume paths from environment variables; an attacker-influenced or operator-typo path becomes a DoS vector.

What goes wrong: availability. A trust-anchor loader that hangs or gets OOM-killed on a malformed file prevents the process from starting / refreshing trust state. For long-running validators (TLS servers, signing services) this is a real defect class — the equivalent class in image loaders has shipped multiple CVEs.

Engineering basis (not theoretical):
- rustls-native-certs and pyca/cryptography both apply explicit upper bounds on trust-store file size.
- Trust-anchor files in the wild: Debian ca-certificates.crt is ~200 KB; Mozilla full bundle is ~250 KB; any path returning > a few MB is almost certainly wrong.
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 names "cache-friendly result types" but the cost of unbounded fs::read happens before the result exists.

Fix: introduce a documented size cap (suggest 64 MiB as a forgiving default; principled is < 16 MiB). Return Error::Io(IoFailure { kind: ErrorKind::FileTooLarge, ... }) or a new typed variant when exceeded. Provide an explicit opt-in (e.g. from_pem_file_with_cap(path, cap) or from_pem_file_unbounded) for callers who genuinely need to bypass.

Threat-model framing: this is not a remote-attacker vulnerability — paths are deployment config. But it is a hard-to-diagnose availability defect that a Tier-1 1.0 loader should not ship. Defense-in-depth: gate the read, not just the parse.

Scope of fix: pkix-truststore. Does not touch pkix-path. Compatible with the no-baked-trust-data stance.

Related: not the same defect class as PKIX-tit4.1 (which is fail-open semantics in cert content); this is fail-OOM in transport.
title: from_pem_file / from_der_file: no size cap on fs::read, allows memory-DoS via /dev/zero or oversized file
